items.text: After months of delay, company Eviation debuted its all-electric aircraft named Alice. The prototype flew for eight minutes above central Washington, US. The plane can carry nine passengers and one or two pilots, and it’s powered by 21,500 small Tesla-style battery cells. The batteries weigh just over 4 tonnes, and they make up half the weight of the aircraft. According to the company, the plane significantly reduces noise, and it costs a fraction to operate, compared to light jets or high-end turboprops . Eviation hopes to use a 30-minute charge for an hour-long flight. The technology is very new, and the hope is to develop a zero-emission and sustainable era in aviation. However, at this moment, Eviation is uncertain if it can make money, which is necessary to become a common way of air travel. Difficult words: debut (to appear or perform in public for the first time), prototype (the first example of something), turboprop (a jet engine that uses a turbine). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

US company Eviation made the first-ever fully electric plane. Last week, the plane called Alice took off, and the first flight lasted eight minutes. The plane can carry nine passengers and two pilots. 21,500 small batteries power the flight. They weigh 4 tonnes which are a half the weight of the plane. Eviation hopes to charge the batteries in 30 minutes for an hour-long flight. The technology is very new. Eviation says that its planes will make no gases at all. The plane is also much quieter than normal planes, and it is a lot cheaper to run. People do not know if electric planes will become a common way of travel, as the technology is very expensive. Difficult words: charge (to store electrical energy in a battery), technology (methods and devices), common (usual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US company Eviation makes a special plane. It is the first fully electric plane. The plane is called Alice. Last week, it takes off in Washington, US. The flight is eight minutes long. Nine passengers and two pilots can be on the plane. The plane is very quiet. It makes almost no gases. 21,500 batteries power the plane. They weigh 4 tonnes. They are a half of the plane’s weight . The plane is very different. It is cheap to fly the plane. Nobody knows if electric planes will be a normal way to travel. The work to make them are very expensive. Difficult words: passenger (a person who travels by plane, bus, and so on), weigh (to be heavy), weight (heaviness). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Builders found a 74-year-old Christmas letter by accident in England when they were tearing down an old chimney. They said that they normally find old newspapers, matchboxes, cigarettes or boxes but nothing like this. One of the builders posted a picture of the letter on Facebook to show how times have changed – kids today ask a lot more than just chalk, slippers and any toy that Santa had to spare . Since the letter was online, the now-grown-up little boy who wrote the letter got in touch. Although the boy’s letter may not have been answered all those years ago, the builders decided in the Christmas spirit to gift him those presents that he longed for when he was a little boy. Difficult words: spare (if you can spare something, you do not need it), spirit (feeling). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Builders were tearing down an old chimney in a house in England when they found a letter. A little boy about 73 years ago addressed the letter to Father Christmas (Santa). The boy wanted chalk, house shoes, and any toy that Santa had to spare . The builders were surprised to find this letter in the chimney. They also could see that children ask for a lot more these days. The builders put a picture of the letter on Facebook. Surprisingly, the person who wrote the letter contacted them and met with them. The builders gave the old man what he wanted all those years ago. Difficult words: tear down (to destroy), chimney (a pipe through which smoke from a fire leaves a building), spare (if you can spare something, you do not need it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A boy writes to Father Christmas (Santa). He asks for some things in the letter. He puts the letter in his home’s chimney . Father Christmas never gets the letter. It stays in the chimney. Seventy-four years later, builders tear down the chimney. They find the letter. They are surprised . They take a picture of it. They put the picture on Facebook. An old man sees the picture. He contacts the builders. The old man is that little boy! It is his letter. The old man meets the builders. The builders give him the things that he wanted from the letter. Difficult words: chimney (a tall round or rectangular thing where smoke from a fire goes up and leaves a building), tear down (to destroy, to break), surprised (if something special happens, it can surprise you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Tuesday, unexplained leaks in two Russian gas pipelines churned up the Baltic Sea with bubbles. The pipelines are important in the growing energy war between Europe and Russia, and the incident undermined the continent’s energy security. Three separate leaks happened on the Nord Stream 1 and 2 pipelines, and seismologists in Sweden and Denmark reported two sharp spikes in undersea activity; the spikes indicated possible explosions. Several European leaders raised concerns about possible infrastructure sabotage . The steel pipelines have a wall of 4.1 centimeters, and the wall has steel-reinforced concrete up to 11 centimeters thick. Each section of the pipe weighs 11 tonnes, which increases to 25 tonnes after the concrete is applied. Sections of the pipelines are between 80 and 110 meters deep. Therefore, a submarine didn’t likely cause the explosions, as submarines are easily detected in the shallow Baltic waters. Europe started an investigation into the leaks, and Sweden launched a probe into the possible sabotage. Difficult words: churn up (to disturb a liquid), undermine (to weaken), sabotage (to deliberately destroy or damage something, especially for political or military advantage). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In early September, Russia shut down Nord Stream 1, an important European gas pipeline. The action was to answer the West’s sanctions of Russia over the war in Ukraine. Nord Stream 1 and 2 transported Russian gas to Europe, and they were very important for Europe’s energy security . On Tuesday, Danish and Swedish scientists detected activity in the Baltic Sea, which maybe were explosions. Later, the Danish military found a big area of gas bubbles near the Nord Stream 1 and 2 pipes. Some European leaders said that the activity was sabotage , and Sweden started to investigate the incidents. The Baltic Sea was between 80 and 110 meters deep, which wasn’t enough for submarines. A submarine probably didn’t cause the damage by accident. Difficult words: sanction (a consequence for a country which breaks international laws), energy security (the situation of enough energy for people and businesses), sabotage (international damage for political or military reasons). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nord Stream 1 and 2 are pipes. They move Russian gas to Europe. Russian gas is very important for Europe. Without it, Europe has energy problems for homes and factories. Russia goes to war in Ukraine. Then Russia gets sanctions from other countries. Gas becomes very expensive. Last month, Russia stops Nord Stream 1. On Tuesday, scientists see activity near Nord Stream 1 and 2. Maybe explosions happen. Bubbles of gas show in the Baltic Sea. The bubbles come if the pipes leak. Gas is coming out from the pipes. Some European leaders say that the incident is a sabotage. Sabotage is an action to break the pipes on purpose . Swedish officials start to investigate what happens. Difficult words: sanction (a punishment for a country which breaks laws), on purpose (with a clear plan to do something), investigate (to find the truth about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For the first time, a cosmic collision happened between a spacecraft and a space rock, millions of kilometers from Earth. NASA showed video of the successful crash of an unmanned spaceship into an asteroid called Dimorphos, a rock the size of a football stadium. The refrigerator-sized shuttle smashed into the asteroid at 22,500 km/h, and it altered the rock’s velocity by a fraction of a second. The historic defense test proves humanity’s ability to stop a cosmic object from destroying our planet. The theory is that the smallest changes in speed and direction can have massive effects on an object’s path through space. The asteroid wasn’t heading for Earth; however, scientists said that people should be reassured to know a planetary defense solution exists. Difficult words: alter (to change slightly), velocity (speed), defense (protection against attack or harm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

For the first time, NASA tested a crash a spacecraft into an asteroid. The crash happened millions of kilometers from Earth. The asteroid wasn’t traveling towards Earth, so it wasn’t dangerous. NASA wanted to prove that people were able to stop an asteroid from crashing into our planet. The spacecraft was as big as a fridge, and it hit an asteroid the size of a football stadium. The speed of the spacecraft was 22,500 km/h. Scientists said that the test showed that people can to stop an object which could destroy our planet. If people changed the speed and direction of the object far enough from Earth, the object’s path change. Difficult words: prove (to show that something exists or is possible), speed (how fast something is), direction (the position towards which something or someone moves). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People worry that an object from space can hit our planet. Scientists look for ideas to stop such an object. One possible idea is to crash into the object. The object has to be far. Then its path will change. It will not hit Earth. Last week, NASA does a test. It sends a spacecraft to space. The spacecraft hits an asteroid. The asteroid is as big as a football stadium. The spacecraft is as big as a fridge. The speed of the spacecraft is 22,500 km/h. The test is successful. The asteroid changes its path a little. This news is very good. People can do something about real danger . Difficult words: path (the way how something moves), speed (how fast something is), danger (a situation which is not safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In northern France in coal mine areas, the latest trend is growing the so-called Charbonnay wine. The wine is a new activity induced by climate change in one of the country’s coldest areas. Winemakers say that heatwaves are bad for growing grapes; however, heat is good. Vines are planted on the spoil tips or piles of accumulated mine waste. Winemakers believe miners proud can be to know that good wine can be produced on the spoil tips of the area’s history, and they have left a mark on many people. Charbonnay is a play on words, as it combines the traditional grape variety of chardonnay with the word ‘charbon’ which means coal in French. In 2018, wineries sold the first bottles mainly to locals and small stores. Due to increasing temperatures, wineries expert to triple production compared to 2021. Difficult words: trend (a development or popular thing), induce (to lead to some action or condition), accumulate (to collect something gradually). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Winemakers in northern France are making a new type of wine. The wine is called Charbonnay, which is a joke on the words chardonnay and charbon. Chardonnay is a famous wine grape, and charbon is the French word for coal. Winemakers grow grapes on spoil tips. These things are piles of material which people leave after they work in a coal mine . Northern France is a cold area, but thanks to climate change, it is getting warmer and is suitable for growing grapes. In 2018, winemakers sold the first bottles of Charbonnay, mostly to local people and small shops. The wine popularity is quickly growing, and it could triple from 2021. Difficult words: mine (to get metals and materials from the earth), suitable (right or correct), triple (to become three times as much or as many). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Charbonnay is a new type of wine from Northern France. Normally, this area is too cold to grow grapes. Then the world gets warmer. Now, people grow grapes there. The name Charbonnay is from two words. The first word is chardonnay. It is a famous grape. The second word is charbon. It is the French word for coal . Winemakers grow the grapes on piles of material. This material comes from coal mines . They are important in this area. People are proud of the new wine. Winemakers sell Charbonnay since 2018. They sell more bottles every year. Difficult words: coal (brown or black rocks which people take from the ground, so they can burn it), mine (to get metals or material from the ground), proud (very happy and pleased). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe’s steel industry faces an uncertain future. The surging energy costs are forcing steel producers to cut output and threaten plant shutdowns. In eastern Belgium, company Aperam switched off some furnaces because its monthly cost for energy is the same as it spent in a year. The company’s production is down by nearly 50%, and over a thousand staff may be temporarily unemployed. Other major producers with many employees have also trimmed output. Germany’s Steel Federation has warned of de-industrialization , and the EU plans to get some money from power producers. However, companies like Aperam do not know how much or when payments may get to them. If this situation lasts for years, Europe will see de-inudstrialization of some industries, and for base metals, it’ll become dependent on imports. These changes matter for the environment, too, as Asian steel makers have lower costs but much higher carbon emissions. Difficult words: furnace (an enclosed structure to heat materials to very high temperatures), trim (to cut), de-industrialization (the reduction of industrial activity in a region). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Aperam is a Belgian-French company which produces steel . Like many other steel producers, the company had big problems in recent months. The prices of electricity and gas grew so much that last month, Aperam spent the same amount of money energy as it spent in the whole year. The company had to switch off some of its furnaces , and it lowered production by 50%. More than a thousand people could lose their jobs, and the situation is similar in other companies, too. The EU wants to get some money back from energy companies, but nobody knows how much money will get to producers. Some experts already worry that some industries could end in Europe. This change would be bad for the companies and also for the environment. Steel producers in Asia make cheaper steel, but they produce a lot more emissions. Difficult words: steel (a hard grey metal to make things like buildings and structures), furnace (a structure to heat metal), industry (companies and their activities in a specific business). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Aperam is a Belgian-French company. It produces steel . The company has big problems now. Many companies have problems. Aperam needs a lot of power. It needs electricity and gas. They are very expensive now. Aperam buys power. It spends the same money for one month as it spends in all last year. The company must switch off some machines. More than one thousand people can lose work. Some experts worry about the situation in Europe. Expensive energy is very bad for companies which produce things. Companies may possibly close. Asian companies can make cheaper steel. Sadly, they produce more emissions than European companies. Difficult words: produce (to make a specific thing), steel (a hard grey material that people use in structures and buildings), emission (smoke and gas from factories and vehicles). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Wednesday, the Russian president Vladimir Putin told his country he would mobilize more troops for the war in Ukraine. Putin said the West had aggressive anti-Russian policies, and it made constant threats against Russia and its people. According to the president, irresponsible politicians in the West discussed giving Ukraine long-range weaponry and missile systems. These items would allow Ukraine to strike Crimea and other Russian regions. Putin said the West encouraged the attack of the Zaporizhzia nuclear power plant, which threatened to unleash a nuclear catastrophe. He said some high-ranking representatives of powerful NATO countries spoke on the possibility of using nuclear weapons against Russia. Putin reminded his people they also had a variety of weapons of destruction and more modern than the NATO countries’ weapons. He explained Russia will use all the weapons at its disposal to protect itself and its people. Difficult words: mobilize (to prepare and organize troops for active service), long-range weaponry (weapons that hit targets at great distances), at disposal (available for someone to use). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Wednesday, Russian president Vladimir Putin spoke to the Russian people on national TV. Putin said that western countries threatened Russia when they delivered weapons to Ukraine. These weapons helped Ukraine fight in Crimea and other parts of Russia. Putin also said that the attack with shells at the Zaporizhzia nuclear power plant was the West’s fault. The attack was very dangerous because it could cause a nuclear disaster. Putin said that some western politicians spoke about using nuclear weapons against Russia. He said that Russia was ready to use its nuclear weapons, too. Some of them were more modern than the western countries’ weapons. Difficult words: threaten (to tell someone that you will do something bad if he doesn’t do what you want), shell (to attack with guns or bombs), nuclear power plant (a factory which makes electricity from tiny objects called atoms). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Wednesday, Russian president Vladimir Putin speaks on TV. He says that he will mobilize more soldiers for the war. New men must become soldiers. They will fight against Ukraine. Putin also speaks about the West . He says that they send weapons to Ukraine. These weapons help Ukraine fight in Crimea and other parts of Russia. They shoot at the Zaporizhzia nuclear power plant . They can start a nuclear emergency. Putin says that leaders of NATO countries want to use nuclear weapons against Russia. Russia has nuclear weapons, too. Some weapons are more modern than the West’s weapons. Difficult words: the West (the UK, US, many European countries, and other countries that believe like they do), mobilize (to prepare soldiers to fight), nuclear power plant (an electricity factory; it breaks very small things called atoms). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Over the death of an Iranian woman in police custody, women removed their hijabs in protests. Iran’s morality police arrested 22-year-old Mahsa Amini for allegedly having some of her hair visible beneath her hijab. She fell into a coma at the police station, and she died three days later. Many people blamed police brutality for the head injuries that killed her. Under the Iranian interpretation of Sharia law, women must cover their hair with a hijab and wear long loose-fitting clothes to disguise their figures. The 1979 revolution instated these rules, and they met with little resistance. As a result, Iranian police force isn’t used to dissent . However, many women of Iran’s traditionally conservative population removed their hijabs. Human rights groups estimate that as many as 31 people died so far in the violent protests. Difficult words: disguise (to change the usual appearance to not recognize a person or thing), instate (to establish), dissent (strong disagreement or difference of opinion). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, Iranian police arrested 22-year-old Mahsa Amini. Police said that the woman wasn’t wearing her hijab properly, and some hair was visible . Police took Mahsa to the police station, where she collapsed. She died in hospital three days later. Officials said that the woman had a heart attack, but some people said that she had serious head injuries because the police beat her. The incident started big protests in Iran. Many women took off their hijabs, which is something nobody could imagine. The Iranian law is very strict, and women must wear hijabs and loose clothes. Human rights groups said that at least 31 people have already died in the protests. Difficult words: hijab (a scarf that Muslim women wear to cover the hair and neck), visible (something that a person can see), loose (clothes which don’t fit closely to the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iranian law says that all women must wear hijabs. A hijab is a scarf. It covers a woman’s hair and neck. Last week, Iranian police arrest a woman. Police say that some of her hair is visible under the hijab. The woman is 22 years old. She faints at the police station. Three days later, she dies in the hospital. Police say that the woman has a heart attack . Sadly, some people believe that police beat the woman. She has serious head injuries . Big protests start in Iran. Women take off their hijab. The behavior is very unusual. Police do not know what to do. Some organizations say that at least 31 people already die in the protests. Difficult words: visible (what you can see), heart attack (when a person’s heart stops working), injury (when someone is hurt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The British icon Sir Elton John has performed on some of the world’s biggest stages. On Friday, a smaller audience of 2,000 people welcomed him at the White House. The audience included teachers, nurses, front line workers , and LGBTQ advocates. Since Joe Biden’s 2020 presidential campaign, the administration has attempted to bring together generations with its choice for music and performance guests. Experts say celebrity endorsements are only effective if the celebrities are familiar, likable, and credible in fans’ eyes. The White House gig was John’s first since he performed with Stevie Wonder at a dinner in 1998, in honor of British Prime Minister Tony Blair. Elton John has long been an advocate for LGBTQ rights and a major activist in the fight against AIDS. President Biden and First Lady Jill Biden welcomed the 75-year-old singer, and they discussed his activism, the power of his music, and his all-round goodness. At the end of the show, Biden surprised John with the National Humanities Medal. Difficult words: front line worker (an employee who provides some essential service to the general public), endorsement (an action that shows support or approval of something or someone), credible (believable or trustworthy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Sir Elton John is one of the greatest British musicians. In 1998, he performed with musician Stevie Wonder at the White House in Washington DC, US. Last week, he returned. 75-year-old John performed in front of 2,000 people, including teachers, nurses, doctors, and LGBTQ advocates . President Joe Biden and First Lady Jill Biden spoke about John’s work, the power of his music, and his goodness . President Biden surprised John with a medal for his activism . Many celebrities perform at the White House. Joe Biden invites celebrities who are popular and trustworthy. For example, the popular South Korean boy band TBS spoke at the White House to support the COVID-19 vaccine, and they also spoke about crimes against Asian communities in the US. Difficult words: LGBTQ advocate (a person who supports the lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender community), goodness (when someone is a good person), activism (activities to achieve political or social changes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sir Elton John is a British singer and songwriter. He is 75 years old. Last Friday, John performs at the White House in Washington DC, US. In 1998, John performs at the White House for the first time. He performs with musician Stevie Wonder. The show is very big. Last week’s show is much smaller. Only 2,000 people watch John sing. They are doctors, nurses and teachers. They are also people who support the LGBTQ community . John gets a medal from President Joe Biden. The medal is a surprise for John. Biden and his wife speak about John’s work and good personality . Difficult words: perform (to sing or play in front of other people), LGBTQ community (gay, lesbian, bisexual, and transgender people), personality (how someone is as a person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists observed some very strange behaviour at the edge of our solar system, and the only possible explanation is that there is another planet which is 9 th . No one has seen this planet, but we have seen its gravitational influence . The scientists modelled the hypothetical planet’s gravitational effects on several known bodies in the region and found a near perfect match, which they described as a jaw-dropping moment. For the observable effects to occur, the planet would be about 10 times bigger than Earth and be much farther than Neptune on a very elliptical orbit . The next scientific discovery now remains to observe the planet directly. Difficult words: observe (to watch), influence (power), body (space object), jaw-dropping (amazing), elliptical (like an ellipse – narrow circle), orbit (a long, circular journey). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists have some new and exciting information. They found the ninth planet in the solar system. It is 10 times bigger than Earth and 20 times farther away from the sun than Earth. However, scientists have not seen the planet yet. They only saw its influence on part of the solar system. They know that the planet is there; they just need to find it. If the planet is real, its orbit is very elliptical . Difficult words: influence (power), orbit (the journey which a planet travels around something), elliptical (like an ellipse – a flat circle). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists have some new information. They say that there is a ninth planet in our solar system . The planet is 10 times bigger than Earth . It is 20 times farther away from the sun than Earth. We cannot see the planet, but we can watch how it moves. Experts are looking for the planet. They know that it is there. They must only find it. Difficult words: solar system (our sun and the 9 planets around it), Earth (our planet), farther (a longer way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Argentina, some fields are test sites for the wheat strain HB4, the first transgenic wheat with global government approvals. A local business developed the strain, and supporters say that the wheat could stop food crises with improvement in wheat yield . HB4 endures better when it has little water, which makes it stronger to drought. Recent events raised fears about the future of food production; the events included historic droughts in China, the US, and Europe and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, a major wheat producer. However, some people warn that genetically modified wheat could affect non-genetically modified wheat. Then international markets could ban wheat supply over contamination fears, which could negatively impact Argentina’s economy. Argentina has approved the business of HB4, and the strain has also gained approvals in Brazil, Nigeria, and Australia. Difficult words: strain (a new type of plant or animal), transgenic (containing one or more genes from another type of plant or animal), yield (a produced or grown amount of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Farmers in Argentina are testing a special strain of wheat called HB4. It is the first genetically modified wheat. Ukraine is one of the biggest global growers of wheat, and when Russia attacked Ukraine, the country couldn’t sell its wheat. The new strain could grow in other parts of the world, too. Big droughts happen in many parts of the world; they inspire scientists to develop stronger plants. HB4 needs less water to grow, therefore, it can help solve the drought problems. Some experts worry that the new strain of wheat will mix with normal wheat. They are afraid that international markets may not want the wheat, which could be a problem for Argentina. Brazil, Nigeria, and Australia are other countries to approve the new strain of wheat. Difficult words: strain (a specific kind of an animal or plant), genetically modified (after scientists change the smallest parts in something to make a new thing), drought (a long time without rain). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Farmers in Argentina are testing a new type of wheat. This wheat is genetically modified. This type of science changes some information inside a plant. The change makes a new plant. The new wheat is called HB4. It can grow with little rain. It is very important. Big droughts are happening in the world. Ukraine is one of the biggest growers of wheat in the world. A war starts in Ukraine with Russia. Then Ukraine can’t sell its wheat. Many countries need wheat to make food. The new wheat can grow in other parts of the world. It can grow in unusual places. Some people worry. They say that the new wheat will mix with other wheat. The new wheat can contaminate the other wheat stock . It can make a bad problem for Argentina’s business. Difficult words: drought (a long time without rain), contaminate (to make dirty), stock (a large amount of something to sell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In New York’s American Museum of Natural History, there is a giant herbivore Titanosaur spanning 37 metres. It is so big that it cannot even fit inside the institute’s fossil hall – its long neck and head poke out of the room, offering a surprise greeting to visitors. Palaeontologists think that the dinosaur, which roamed the forests around 100 million years ago, would have weighed about 70 tonnes; that is the weight of ten elephants. People first discovered the species in 2014 in Argentina’s Patagonia region. Palaeontologists excavated the Titanosaur in the Argentinian desert after a rancher gave them a tip, who noticed the fossils on his land. The Titanosaur was temporarily on display in New York, and around five million visitors come to the museum each year, proving that dinosaurs are still proper celebrities. Difficult words: herbivore (a dinosaur that feeds on plants), spanning (being long), poke out (be out and to be visible), palaeontologist (a scientist who studies bones), roam (live, move around), excavate (dig out). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Argentina in 2014, people first discovered Titanosaurs, which are dinosaurs. They lived in the forests of Patagonia 100 million years ago. People excavated one Titanosaur and moved it to New York. It is now in the American Museum of Natural History. The dinosaur is 37 metres tall and it does not even fit into the fossil hall. Its neck and its head run through the doorway into another room. Around five million visitors a year will see the skeleton of the dinosaur. The titanosaur ate plants and it weighed around 70 tonnes – that is like 10 elephants. Difficult words: excavate (to dig out), fossil (pieces of animals or plants that turned into rocks), skeleton (all of the bones of the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Titanosaurs lived 100 million years ago. They lived in Argentina. They ate plants. They were 70 tonnes heavy. That is like ten elephants. People find a titanosaur. They move it to New York. The dinosaur goes into a museum. It is in a hall. It is longer than the hall. It does not fit inside completely. Its neck and its head run through the doorway into another room. Every year, five million people visit this museum. Difficult words: ate (past of “eat”), doorway (a space in a wall to walk through and where a door goes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After 70 years, eight radio-collared African cheetahs stepped onto the grassland of Kuno National Park in central India; the big cats disappeared from the wild here. The animals made an 8,000-kilometer journey from Namibia, and the journey was the first for wild cheetahs to move across continents. The cheetahs will run through 5,000 square kilometers of forest and grassland, and they’ll share the landscape with other animals. Next month, 12 more cheetahs from South Africa are expected to join them. The high-profile project drew criticism from scientists and conservationists , who say the vanity project ignores the fact the African cheetah isn’t native to the Indian subcontinent. Some people also worry that the animals won’t have enough space to roam, and predators or people will eventually kill them. Difficult words: high-profile (attraction of attention or publicity), conservationist (a person who actively protects the environment and wildlife), vanity (worthless or ridiculous). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

70 years ago, cheetahs disappeared from India’s wild. Now, they finally returned. Eight cheetahs traveled 8,000 kilometers from Namibia, and they will now live in a national park in central India. The park’s area is 5,000 square kilometers, and the cheetahs will live there with many other animals. 12 more cheetahs will arrive next month from South Africa to join them. Some scientists and conservationists are not happy with this project. They say that African cheetahs shouldn’t live on the Indian subcontinent . They also say that the animals won’t have enough space and that other animals or people could kill them. Difficult words: disappear (to be gone and people cannot find you), conservationist (a person who protects the natural world), subcontinent (a large part of a continent). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The cheetah is the fastest land animal on earth. In the past, cheetahs live in India. They disappear 70 years ago. Last week, cheetahs return to India. Eight animals travel 8,000 kilometers from Namibia. They will live in a national park . The park has 5,000 square kilometers. Many other animals live there. 12 more cheetahs will come there. They will come from South Africa next month. Some people criticize the expensive project. They say that it is not good that African animals live in India. Some people also worry that other animals or people will kill the cheetahs. Difficult words: disappear (to be gone), national park (a large area of land where animals and plants are safe), criticize (to say why something is not good). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Sunday, Hurricane Fiona had made landfall at Puerto Rico; the storm caused the entire island to be without power, and it threatened catastrophic flooding. The hurricane started landslides and mudslides with its winds of over 135 kmph. Authorities closed all ports and canceled all flights out of the main airport. Puerto Rico’s governor said the country’s power grid remained fragile since 2017’s Hurricane Maria hit the country, which caused the largest blackout in US history. Many people hadn’t prepared for Maria because they thought nothing bad would happen. For Hurricane Fiona, they bought power generators to be ready for the storm. Authorities opened shelters, and they urged people to go for cover. As the storm progressed northwest, experts also forecast torrential rains and mudslides for the Dominican Republic. In Amman, the capital of Jordan, rescuers saved a 4-month-old baby from the rubble of a collapsed four-story residential building. Rescuers pulled the mother Israa Raed from the wreckage; she distributed sweets outside a hospital for the victims. Over 10 people were declared dead, and the death toll still increased. However, after hours of scouring the debris, rescue teams were found some survivors. People who luckily survived were in shock from the collapse, and they said that the floor gave way beneath them. People do not know the collapse’s cause, but police arrested three people, including the building owner. The building’s neighborhood was known for its cafes, bars, and artistic venues, and it was popular with both expatriates and locals. Difficult words: death toll (the number of dead people in an accident or disaster), scour (to search a place carefully), expatriate (a person who lives outside his native country). Since an economic crisis started three years ago, Lebanon’s banks have locked most depositors out of their savings. Last week on Friday, an armed man entered a bank in Beirut, and he demanded his savings. A large crowd of people gathered outside, and they cheered the man. He said he wouldn’t leave until the bank paid him his money. Several other armed customers stormed at least five banks to demand access to their own funds. Such holdups have become increasingly frequent as the country sinks deeper into the economic crisis. Banks were forced to push strict limits on currency withdrawals to avoid economic failure. The interior minister warned that the attacks destroyed order in the country, but many people believe that the desperate depositors are folk heroes. Difficult words: depositor (a person who keeps money in a bank), holdup (a robbery with the use of threats or violence), folk (related to ordinary people). Swiss tennis star Roger Federer announced that he would retire after next week’s Laver Cup in London, UK. Many people regard Federer as the greatest male player to swing a tennis racket because he has won 20 Grand Slam titles. With his artistry and grace, he dominated men’s tennis for years. In 2003, he won his first grand slam title at Wimbledon, and he took the sport to new levels. After losing at last year’s Wimbledon, Federer planned to play another match, but a knee injury stopped him. However, his fans still believed that he could return for one last golden farewell . In his latest Instagram post, Federer said that at 41 years old, he’d played more than 1,500 matches over 24 years. Tennis was his lifelong passion, but he recognized that the time came to end his competitive career. Federer’s career includes eight Wimbledon titles, five US Open titles, six Australian crowns and a single French Open title. He also holds the record for 237 consecutive weeks as world number one. Difficult words: dominate (to be the most important person in something), golden farewell (a positive occasion to depart or say goodbye), consecutive (one event or activity after another without an interruption). To save energy, Paris, France, will switch off the Eiffel Tower’s lights hours earlier than normal. The Eiffel Tower is among the most visited monuments in the world, and it’s currently illuminated until 1 AM with an elaborate lighting system to give it a golden glow. In addition, the monument twinkles for five minutes on the hour from nightfall, thanks to 20,000 flashing bulbs. The Paris city hall is going to propose that the tower falls dark at 11:45 PM when the final visitors leave, so it’ll no longer twinkle at midnight. The current energy crisis is the reason for the change, and it’s an example for the reduction of city illumination. The monument’s night-time lights accounts for 4% of the its total annual energy use. The city hall is also going to lower the water temperature in municipal pools and delay heat to public buildings to save energy this winter. Difficult words: elaborate (detailed and carefully arranged), twinkle (to shine repeatedly strongly and then weakly), municipal (the government of a city or town). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Difficult words: bulb (a glass device which uses electricity to make light), twinkle (to shine strongly and then weakly), energy crisis (little or expensive energy in a large place). Major US credit card companies are reclassifying purchases at gun stores and ammunition shops to reveal gun purchases. For the first time, Visa, American Express, and MasterCard will start the plan; it will separate gun and ammunition purchases from other kinds of shopping. Previously, these companies classified guns and ammunition as general merchandise . Over the last several years, gun sales have increased, and they increase even more whenever the US government talks about gun control. In the last two years, the FBI reported over 78 million background checks for gun purchases, which was more than in any two-year time period since records started in 1998. Authorities hope that the new classification for credit card purchases will differentiate people who buy a gun for safety from people who buy a gun to harm someone. Difficult words: merchandise (goods that people buy and sell), classification (the division of things into groups according to their type), differentiate (to recognize the difference between things). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
